newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cen bank says begins limiting Lombard access.
newsitem.headline: Czech cen bank says begins limiting Lombard access.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) on Tuesday said it had begun to impose limits on banks' access to the last resort lending facility, the Lombard rate, to an unspecified portion of a bank's capital.
CNB spokesman Martin Svehla told Reuters the restriction applied equally to all foreign and Czech banks with a licence to operate in the country.
"We intend only to regulate somehow the access to the Lombard credit, and the intention is for equal (access) to the Lombard (based on) the capital of a bank," Svehla said.

"I deny that we are making any kind of difference between foreign and domestic banks all of them having a licence, our treatment is the same -- the Lombard credit can be given adequately to a portion of capital," he added.

But Stefan Balgavy of Commerzbank said his bank, which operates as a licensed branch, was denied access to the lending facility outright since a branch's capital is virtually non-existent locally, but calculated instead through its parent bank.
"I don't understand where they are going with this. It appears as though banks are not being treated equally," he said.
